# dlarrk

> Computes one eigenvalue of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix to suitable accuracy.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarrk from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlarrk';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarrk( N, iw, gl, gu, d, strideD, E2, strideE2, pivmin, reltol, w, werr ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of columns |
| `iw` | `integer` | in |  |  | the index of the eigenvalues to be returned. |
| `gl` | `number` | in |  |  | an upper and a lower bound on the eigenvalue. |
| `gu` | `number` | in |  |  | an upper and a lower bound on the eigenvalue. |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `d` |
| `E2` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `E2` |
| `pivmin` | `number` | in |  |  | minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence |
| `reltol` | `number` | in |  |  | relative tolerance for convergence |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output array for the computed eigenvalue |
| `werr` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output array for the error bound |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the tridiagonal matrix T. $N \ge 0$.
- `iw`: The index of the eigenvalues to be returned.
- `gu`: An upper and a lower bound on the eigenvalue.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `E2`: The (n-1) squared off-diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `pivmin`: The minimum pivot allowed in the Sturm sequence for T.
- `reltol`: The minimum relative width of an interval. When an interval is narrower than `RELTOL` times the larger (in magnitude) endpoint, then it is considered to be sufficiently small, i.e., converged. Note: this should always be at least radix\*machine $\epsilon$.
- `werr`: The error bound on the corresponding eigenvalue approximation in W.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarrk.ndarray(
    N,
    iw, gl, gu,
    D, strideD, offsetD,
    E2, strideE2, offsetE2,
    pivmin, reltol,
    w,
    werr
) → info: integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `iw` | `integer` | in |  |  | 1-based index of the eigenvalue to compute |
| `gl` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound of the initial interval |
| `gu` | `number` | in |  |  | upper bound of the initial interval |
| `D` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal elements (length `N`) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `D` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `D` |
| `E2` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | squared off-diagonal elements (length `N-1`) |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `E2` |
| ↳ `offsetE2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `E2` |
| `pivmin` | `number` | in |  |  | minimum pivot in the Sturm sequence |
| `reltol` | `number` | in |  |  | relative tolerance for the returned eigenvalue |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output array for the computed eigenvalue (length >= 1) |
| `werr` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output array for the error bound (length >= 1) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the tridiagonal matrix T. $N \ge 0$.
- `iw`: The index of the eigenvalues to be returned.
- `gu`: An upper and a lower bound on the eigenvalue.
- `D`: The n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `E2`: The (n-1) squared off-diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `pivmin`: The minimum pivot allowed in the Sturm sequence for T.
- `reltol`: The minimum relative width of an interval. When an interval is narrower than `RELTOL` times the larger (in magnitude) endpoint, then it is considered to be sufficiently small, i.e., converged. Note: this should always be at least radix\*machine $\epsilon$.
- `werr`: The error bound on the corresponding eigenvalue approximation in W.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: status code (0 = success, -1 = did not converge)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: Eigenvalue converged
-   `= -1`: Eigenvalue did NOT converge

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlarrk()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARRK`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlarrk.f).
-   `dlarrk` is a helper routine used internally by `dlarrd` to refine individual eigenvalues via bisection on the Sturm count of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix.
-   The eigenvalue is refined within the interval `[gl, gu]`, which is widened slightly to ensure the target eigenvalue is bracketed.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlarrk from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlarrk';

// 3x3 symmetric tridiagonal matrix with D=[2,2,2], E=[1,1], E2=[1,1]

// Eigenvalues: 2-sqrt(2), 2, 2+sqrt(2)
const d = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 2.0, 2.0 ] );
const e2 = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0 ] );
const w = new Float64Array( 1 );
const werr = new Float64Array( 1 );

let info = dlarrk( 3, 1, 0.0, 4.0, d, 1, e2, 1, 1.0e-18, 1.0e-12, w, werr );
console.log( 'First eigenvalue: %d (error: %d, info: %d)', w[ 0 ], werr[ 0 ], info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

info = dlarrk( 3, 2, 0.0, 4.0, d, 1, e2, 1, 1.0e-18, 1.0e-12, w, werr );
console.log( 'Second eigenvalue: %d (error: %d, info: %d)', w[ 0 ], werr[ 0 ], info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

info = dlarrk( 3, 3, 0.0, 4.0, d, 1, e2, 1, 1.0e-18, 1.0e-12, w, werr );
console.log( 'Third eigenvalue: %d (error: %d, info: %d)', w[ 0 ], werr[ 0 ], info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARRK`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARRK computes one eigenvalue of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix T to suitable accuracy. This is an auxiliary code to be called from DSTEMR.

To avoid overflow, the matrix must be scaled so that its largest element is no greater than overflow\*\*(1/2) \* underflow\*\*(1/4) in absolute value, and for greatest accuracy, it should not be much smaller than that.

See W. Kahan "Accurate Eigenvalues of a Symmetric Tridiagonal Matrix", Report CS41, Computer Science Dept., Stanford University, July 21, 1966.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
